The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Bridge

    Covered Bridges

    Their towers were part of the city’s 13th-century defences. The bridges once had wooden roofs, which gave them their name, and were largely rebuilt in the 19th century.

    Look for

    Stand on a bridge and count the channels: here the Ill splits into several arms, each once guarded by a tower.

  2. 02
    Civic building · 1999

    European Parliament

    The Louise Weiss building opened in 1999, named after a French journalist and member of the European Parliament. Members meet here for most of their plenary sessions.

    Look for

    The top of the round tower looks unfinished on one side. It is often said to stand for Europe itself, still a work in progress.

  3. 03
    Neighbourhood

    La Petite France

    Tanners, millers and fishermen once worked along these channels. The name comes from a 16th-century hospice for men with syphilis, then known as the French disease.

    Look for

    On the Maison des Tanneurs and its neighbours, look for open galleries under the steep roofs, where hides were hung to dry.

  4. 04
    Palace · 1742

    Palais Rohan

    Robert de Cotte designed it for the prince-bishops of the Rohan family, and it was finished in 1742. It now holds the museums of fine arts, decorative arts and archaeology.

  5. 05
    Park

    Parc de l’Orangerie

    The Pavillon Joséphine in the park is named after Napoleon’s empress. White storks, the symbol of Alsace, have been bred and protected here for decades.

    Look for

    The timber-framed farmhouse by the lake, the Buerehiesel, is centuries old; it was moved here and rebuilt for an exhibition in 1895.

  6. 06
    Square

    Place Kléber

    It is named after General Jean-Baptiste Kléber, who was born in Strasbourg, and his remains lie in a vault beneath the statue. In winter a giant Christmas tree stands here.

    Look for

    The long classical building on the north side is the Aubette. Its interiors were redesigned in 1928 by Theo van Doesburg, Sophie Taeuber-Arp and Jean Arp.

  7. 07
    Square

    Place de la République

    It was laid out after 1871, when Strasbourg became part of the German Empire, as the heart of the new Neustadt. Its war memorial shows a mother holding two dying sons, one who fought for France and one for Germany.

    Look for

    The heavy domed building on the square is the Palais du Rhin, built as an imperial palace for the German emperor.

  8. 08
    Church · 1439

    Strasbourg Cathedral

    Its spire was completed in 1439, and from 1647 to 1874 it was the tallest building in the world. Inside, the astronomical clock sets its figures moving every day at half past noon.

    Look for

    Near the clock, find the Pillar of Angels: a slender column ringed with carved angels blowing trumpets and the Evangelists, around the Last Judgement.

  9. 09
    Viewpoint

    Vauban Dam

    It was built at the end of the 17th century to plans by Vauban. By closing its sluices, the city could flood the land to the south against an attacking army.

    Look for

    Inside the dam’s long gallery stand weathered stone statues and carvings taken down from the city’s old buildings.
